selectivity --- a class now certified nonempty, with dynamical selection
the open question --- posed in an exact finite arena, the 32-dimensional
admissible condensate space splitting evenly into sixteen blind and
sixteen flipping directions (\texttt{hchiprime\_probes.py},
\texttt{condensate\_space\_probes.py}); the Standard-Model chirality
identification remains conditional on it (SM §4.8), with the grading
identification and both blindness certifications probe-backed. Section
19.3 also takes up two framework-specific meta-questions: whether the
discrete structural residue is genuinely non-tautological (§19.3.6) ---
now \emph{resolved} by a three-tier classification of the framework's
results, which is the section's main conceptual addition and reframes
the framework's overall claim as a tight compression of physics rather
than a derivation of it from first principles --- and the radiative
stability of emergent Lorentz invariance in the rotational sector
(§19.3.7), where a symmetry argument and a first numerical test support
protection, with specific questions remaining.

Section 19.4 closes the chapter with a summary table and a note on what
the framework does \emph{not address}: specific experimental anomalies
(muon \(g-2\), \(B\)-physics, \(W\) mass) at scales where the
framework's \(\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^2 E^2)\) corrections are
unobservable, condensed matter and many-body phenomena that are problems
within the derived QFT rather than at the framework level, and the
framework's principled scope limit on the hard problem of consciousness
(developed in Chapter 18 §18.10).

The chapter functions as a systematic reference resource. Readers
wanting to understand how the framework engages a specific open problem
can find the framework's status and the cross-reference to where the
relevant content is developed. The chapter is not a substitute for the
detailed treatments in Chapters 5 through 18; it is an inventory making
the framework's reach explicit.

A note on tone. The inventory is honest about the framework's actual
content. Where the framework resolves a problem, the inventory states
the resolution and provides the cross-reference; where the framework
only partially addresses a problem, the inventory marks the partial
status and identifies what remains open; where the framework does not
address a problem at all, the inventory acknowledges this rather than
overstating the framework's reach. The closing summary table makes the
distribution of statuses explicit.

\hypertarget{resolutions-and-partial-treatments}{%
\subsection{19.2 Resolutions and partial
treatments}\label{resolutions-and-partial-treatments}}

This section develops the framework's claimed resolutions, dissolutions,
and conditional constructions, with quantum gravity as a partially
addressed entry, the black hole information paradox as an unresolved
entry whose information conservation is a premise of the framework's
models and whose Page curve is conditional, and the Born-rule origin and
the strong CP problem alongside them as split-status entries.
Gauge-group origin and generation structure are explicitly conditional
on the carrier bridge rather than counted as closed results.

\hypertarget{the-quantum-gravity-problem}{%
\subsubsection{19.2.1 The quantum gravity
problem}\label{the-quantum-gravity-problem}}

\textbf{Standard status.} The Einstein--Hilbert action is perturbatively
non-renormalizable as a continuum quantum field theory. At low energies
it admits a predictive effective-field-theory expansion with
higher-curvature terms. The microscopic theory of quantum gravity
remains open. \href{https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.50.3874}{Donoghue}

\textbf{Framework status.} The proposed common substratum
\((S,\varphi)\) supplies a setting for a fixed-basis trace-out
representation under its stated conditions (Chapter 1). The
gravitational treatment gives conditional horizon normalizations at G1
and weak-field consistency at G2. Covariant dynamics, the native source
and the continuum or long-wavelength recovery remain open at G3. The
cosmological implications of G4 carry those and their own conditions.
Which level carries the gravitational field of a laboratory mass in an
apparent spatial superposition also remains open (Chapter 7 §7.7). On
the spherical single-link H-link branch, the horizon calibration gives
the proposed physical lattice spacing
\(\epsilon_{\rm lat}=\sqrt{6\sigma}\,l_p\), with \(\sigma\) the entropy
per counted boundary mode. This supplies a proposed microscopic cutoff.
Recovering the observed covariant effective theory and its source at
long wavelengths is a separate requirement at G3.

Chapter 18 §18.5 develops three aspects of the proposal. The
cosmological-constant account requires the open covariant coupling for
vacuum-offset decoupling. In the black-hole account, the underlying
bijection preserves information by premise and the radiation's Page
curve follows under further conditions. The fixed-spacing lattice is a
proposed microscopic description whose long-wavelength matching remains
open.

\emph{Developed in:} Chapters 1, 7, and 18. The three components are
developed in Chapter 7 §7.7 (cosmological constant), Chapter 7 §7.6
(black hole information), and Chapter 18 §18.5 (non-renormalizability
and cumulative case).

\hypertarget{the-cosmological-constant-problem}{%
\subsubsection{19.2.2 The cosmological constant
problem}\label{the-cosmological-constant-problem}}

\textbf{Standard status.} The worst quantitative discrepancy in physics.
Quantum field theory predicts a vacuum energy of order
\(M_{\text{Pl}}^4 \sim 10^{113}\,\text{J/m}^3\), summing zero-point
energies \(\frac{1}{2}\hbar\omega\) over all field modes up to the
Planck cutoff. The observed vacuum energy density is
\(\rho_{\text{obs}} \sim H^2/G \sim 10^{-9}\,\text{J/m}^3\). The ratio
\(10^{122}\) has been treated as a fine-tuning problem requiring an
unknown cancellation mechanism --- a cancellation that must be
re-imposed at each order of perturbation theory.

\textbf{Framework status.} The field-theory zero-point sum and the
supplied Friedmann-scale density belong to different descriptions. Their
scale ratio is of order the de Sitter entropy under the conventions of
Chapter 7 §7.7. The observed vacuum density uses the supplied fraction
\(\Omega_\Lambda\rho_{\rm crit}\). Comparing complete conserved stress
tensors on a common metric with a fixed physical reference cancels a
shared offset in their difference. The native stress or flux map, the
reference source and the response to physical vacuum changes remain open
at G3. {[}GR §6.2{]}

\emph{Developed in:} Chapter 7 §7.7.

\hypertarget{the-nature-of-dark-matter}{%
\subsubsection{19.2.3 The nature of dark
matter}\label{the-nature-of-dark-matter}}

\textbf{Standard status.} About \(27\%\) of the reference cosmological
budget is in a clustering component with negligible electromagnetic
coupling. Cold-dark-matter models can account for this with a particle
species. Direct searches constrain the masses and interactions tested.

\textbf{Framework status.} The boundary displacement proposal uses the
conditional de Sitter temperature ({[}GR §3.2{]}) and the heat input
\(Q=M_Bc^2\) that the open G3 source map would supply. It gives the
critical acceleration \(a_0=cH/6\approx1.1\times10^{-10}\,\text{m/s}^2\)
and the deep-MOND baryonic Tully-Fisher relation \(v^4=GM_BcH/6\), with
\(1/6\) imported from Verlinde. The simple radial interpolation
\(\nu(y)=(1+\sqrt{1+4/y})/2\) gives a fractional correction tending to
zero at large \(g_B\). It compares well with the stated Coma example,
while rich-cluster cores retain a \(1.0\)--\(1.5\times\) residual. The
approximate \(0.059\) eV normal-ordering minimum uses measured
splittings and a negligible lightest neutrino mass (Chapter 8 §8.9). The
Bullet Cluster account assumes the displacement relaxes on a horizon
timescale. The pre-collision pattern and its link to the observed
lensing remain open. Acoustic-cycle averaging and the matter-era
tracking solution motivate a large-scale mechanism. The measured
acoustic peaks require the coupled perturbation calculation with a
native source. The Milky Way outer decline and the reported
high-redshift declining velocities remain in tension with the stated
radial law (Chapter 7 §7.9).

\emph{Developed in:} Chapter 7 §7.9.

\hypertarget{the-nature-of-dark-energy}{%
\subsubsection{19.2.4 The nature of dark
energy}\label{the-nature-of-dark-energy}}

\textbf{Standard status.} Approximately \(68\%\) of the energy budget
drives the universe's accelerated expansion. Whether dark energy is a
cosmological constant (constant in time) or evolving (the running-vacuum
and quintessence proposals) is the subject of active investigation. The
DESI Data Release 2 reports \(2.8\)--\(4.2\sigma\) preference for
evolving dark energy in the \(w_0 w_a\)CDM parameterization, with the
empirical situation in flux as of 2025-2026.

\textbf{Framework status.} The boundary interpretation is a Type II
structural reading. The considered implementation uses conserved matter
and running \(G\). For a smooth vacuum density and \(c=1\), the local
expansion about \(H_0>0\) is
\[\rho_\Lambda(H)=\rho_\Lambda(H_0)+\frac{3\nu}{8\pi G}(H^2-H_0^2)+\mathcal{O}\bigl((H^2-H_0^2)^2\bigr).\]
The local expansion holds for smooth densities generally. The near-null
field estimate \(|\nu_{\rm QFT}|\sim10^{-32}\) has the source and
spectral conditions of {[}GR §7.1{]}. The separate Bertini et al.~fit is
compatible with zero, which is also compatible with \(\Lambda\)CDM. The
DESI DR2 preference quoted above compares \(w_0w_a\)CDM with
\(\Lambda\)CDM. A crossing or running beyond the variation allowed by
the stated near-null model would challenge that model. Its source
attribution remains open.

\emph{Developed in:} Chapter 7 §7.8.

\hypertarget{the-measurement-problem}{%
\subsubsection{19.2.5 The measurement
problem}\label{the-measurement-problem}}

\textbf{Standard status.} What constitutes a measurement? Why does
wave-function collapse occur? Why does the classical world appear
definite? No consensus exists across Copenhagen, Many-Worlds, Bohmian,
QBist, dynamical collapse, and other interpretations.

\textbf{Framework status.} Observer-relative account. In the proposed
deterministic substratum interpretation, the wave function represents an
observer's incomplete information. At the represented fixed-basis level,
measurement conditions on a visible outcome and re-marginalizes the
hidden sector. The exact finite-law correspondence admits that readout
universally (\(S \iff D \iff Q_{\mathrm{fb}}\), {[}Main §3.4{]}); a full
operational completion requires the separately stated matrix setting and
completion conditions (§19.2.12). The ordinary Wigner's-friend
interpretation assigns a definite substratum record and
observer-relative information about it. It does not settle every
measurement protocol or the Frauchiger-Renner certainty and consistency
assumptions. Those require the proposed completion's operational
probabilities and a separate premise analysis.

\emph{Developed in:} Chapter 1, with related content in Chapter 18
§§18.2 and 18.4.

\hypertarget{the-black-hole-information-paradox}{%
\subsubsection{19.2.6 The black hole information
paradox}\label{the-black-hole-information-paradox}}

\textbf{Standard status.} Does black hole evaporation destroy
information? Hawking's 1975 semiclassical calculation produces thermal
radiation that appears to carry no information about the black hole's
initial state; if the radiation is exactly thermal, information is
destroyed when the black hole completes evaporation --- in tension with
quantum mechanics' commitment to unitarity. The AdS/CFT correspondence
and the recent quantum-extremal-surface and entanglement-island programs
suggest information is preserved, but the mechanism in the bulk has been
unclear.

\textbf{Framework status.} Information is conserved by the bijectivity
premise of the framework's models; the paradox is not resolved, and the
Page curve is conditional. In the framework's models \(\varphi\) is
bijective by premise (Chapter 1), so information is never lost from it;
how much of it the radiation carries, bijectivity does not settle. The
Page curve follows, as an average over the cycles of the dynamics, under
the scrambling condition H-scramble and the decoupling condition
H-decouple ({[}GR Appendix A{]}), neither of which is established:
H-scramble carries Popescu-Short-Winter measure concentration to the
orbit of the deterministic substratum dynamics on the full product space
of the black hole and its radiation, whose cycle structure supplies
exact time averages; it fails for every bijection acting on an initial
configuration with the bipartition aligned to the configuration
coordinates, the setting the derivation counts, so the Page value
requires an initial superposition over at least about
\(e^{S_{\text{Page}}}\) configurations (\(S_{\text{Page}}\) the Page
entropy) or a non-aligned bipartition; on a proper energy shell the
value is open. The Page time is
\(t_P = [1 - (\beta/(1+\beta))^{3/2}]\, t_{\text{evap}}\), independent
of mass for a mass-independent emission coefficient, where \(\beta\) is
the radiation's entropy per unit of horizon entropy lost:
\((1 - 2^{-3/2})\, t_{\text{evap}} \approx 0.646\, t_{\text{evap}}\) at
the mode-counting value \(\beta = 1\), and earlier for \(\beta > 1\),
which holds in the semiclassical emission regime defined in Chapter 7
§7.6 and there depends on the species content and the greybody factors.
The derivation runs through a mechanism substantially different from the
quantum-extremal-surface and entanglement-island programs --- cycle
typicality on the configuration space rather than replica wormhole
computation in the gravitational path integral. The conjectured
correspondence ``replica wormholes \(\leftrightarrow\) substratum
cycles'' is suggestive but not yet rigorous; making it precise would
require constructing the gravitational path integral as an effective
description of the substratum dynamics in the appropriate limit. The
generalized second law remains open. The subadditivity bound is relative
to a reference product state. A second law requires both a
horizon--sector entropy identification and monotonicity between times
(§7.6).

\emph{Developed in:} Chapter 7 §7.6.

\hypertarget{the-strong-cp-problem}{%
\subsubsection{19.2.7 The strong CP
problem}\label{the-strong-cp-problem}}

\textbf{Standard status.} Why is the QCD vacuum angle
\(\bar\theta < 10^{-10}\)? Naively, \(\bar\theta\) should be
\(\mathcal{O}(1)\) as a generic parameter of the QCD Lagrangian. The
Peccei-Quinn mechanism (axion) is the leading conventional solution, but
the axion has not been detected despite extensive searches.

\textbf{Framework status.} Not resolved. T-invariance of the substratum
gives \(\theta\in\{0,\pi\}\), not \(\theta=0\): \(\theta\) is periodic
and \(T\) sends \(\theta\to-\theta\), so both are T-invariant points,
and selecting the \(\theta=0\) branch is a separate condition
(\textbf{H-top}). Under the counting hidden prior of a finite model,
reciprocity of the visible transition counts,
\(T_{ij}=T_{\theta j,\theta i}\), holds exactly at every time scale, but
it does not give a T-invariant emergent Hamiltonian: a bipartite \(C_4\)
ring with complex hopping \(z\) has \(|U_{ij}(t)|^2=|U_{ji}(t)|^2\) at
every \(t\) while its loop product \(z^4\) carries a phase no diagonal
rephasing can remove {[}SM, Prop. 20{]}. The Yukawa determinant phase,
and with it \(\bar\theta=\theta+\arg\det(Y_uY_d)\), is therefore not
fixed by the construction {[}SM, Theorem 21{]}. The remaining target is
narrower than full reality: \textbf{H-det}, \(\arg\det(Y_uY_d)=0\) with
the flavor quartets left free --- a mechanism making \(Y_u,Y_d\)
simultaneously real would also force \(J_{\rm CKM}=0\), which is the
falsification control on any proposal. Reciprocal probabilities can hide
genuine loop phases, so detailed balance at the substratum does not kill
weak CP violation, and the observed CKM phase is compatible with the
construction as solution-level data. What the construction establishes
is what time-reversal symmetry does and does not fix; what it does not
have is a mechanism for H-top or H-det. A reported computation on the
staggered reconstruction, not available for verification, found that an
octahedral-equivariant emergent operator gives \(J=0\) and that
restoring the observed \(J\) would require octahedral breaking far above
the rotational bounds; it is recorded as an unverified tension for the
flavor sector {[}SM §5.5{]}.

\emph{Developed in:} Chapter 6 §6.3.

\hypertarget{the-hierarchy-problem}{%
\subsubsection{19.2.8 The hierarchy
problem}\label{the-hierarchy-problem}}

\textbf{Standard status.} Why is the Higgs mass (\(\sim 125\) GeV) so
much lighter than the Planck mass (\(\sim 10^{19}\) GeV)? Radiative
corrections in a generic effective field theory should drive \(m_H\) to
the cutoff unless an unknown mechanism --- supersymmetry, compositeness,
extra dimensions, or anthropic selection --- protects the Higgs mass
from quadratic divergences. None of the conventional protection
mechanisms has been confirmed empirically.

\textbf{Framework status.} The discrete pairing of the two singlet
corners motivates composite-Higgs protection. The lattice is a proposed
microscopic cutoff, with long-wavelength matching required separately
(§19.2.1). Cutoff insensitivity of \(m_H^2\) requires a continuous
broken symmetry, a Higgs Goldstone direction and a quantitative
calculation of explicit breaking (SM §8.8). The hierarchy \(v\ll f\)
also remains open.

The singlet-taste construction accommodates the supplied Higgs doublet
in the \(E\) projection (SM Theorem 11). The equivariant condensate has
the stated stabilizer on its carrier and condensate branch. Deriving the
physical masses and their protection requires the remaining dynamical
steps (Chapter 6 §6.6).

\emph{Developed in:} Chapter 6 §6.6.

\hypertarget{the-origin-of-the-gauge-group}{%
\subsubsection{19.2.9 The origin of the gauge
group}\label{the-origin-of-the-gauge-group}}

\textbf{Standard status.} Why
\(\mathrm{SU}(3) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{U}(1)\)? Why these
multiplicities for the matter content? Why this specific representation
structure? The conventional account treats the Standard Model gauge
group as empirically determined input rather than derived from any
deeper principle.

\textbf{Framework status.} \textbf{Conditional physical-carrier
construction with an exact geometric core.} The six signed
nearest-neighbor links of the simple-cubic graph form an exact
six-dimensional cubic-group representation and decompose as \((3,2,1)\).
What is \emph{not} presently derived is the identification of this
geometric link representation with the complete physical gauge carrier:
that is H-link, with the single-copy clause \(m=1\) giving \(K=6\); the
condensate-stabilizer route additionally uses H-cust. Conditional on
those named bridges and the later chirality/matter hypotheses, the
anomaly and representation calculations recover the Standard-Model gauge
structure and hypercharges. The origin of the geometric \((3,2,1)\)
decomposition is therefore resolved; the physical-carrier origin is an
explicit open bridge.

\emph{Developed in:} Chapter 5 (gauge structure) and Chapter 6 (matter
content and quantitative predictions).

\hypertarget{the-generation-puzzle}{%
\subsubsection{19.2.10 The generation
puzzle}\label{the-generation-puzzle}}

\textbf{Standard status.} Why three generations? Why do all three have
identical gauge quantum numbers but hierarchical masses spanning roughly
five orders of magnitude? The Standard Model accommodates three
generations as empirical input but has no explanation for the
multiplicity or for the mass hierarchy pattern.

\textbf{Framework status.} Partially derived and carrier-conditional. On
the H-link single-copy branch, three candidate sectors arise from the
staggered/cubic taste structure. The \(T_1\) representation of the cubic
group has dimension three, giving three candidate sectors on the
single-copy branch; their identification as physical generations
additionally requires H-spin' and light-spectrum selection. Anomaly
cancellation fixes hypercharges given the observed chiral family
pattern; it does not select that pattern from the link carrier (SM
Theorem 10). Identical gauge quantum numbers follow because all three
generations are copies of the same \(T_1\) irrep. Hierarchical masses
follow because the specific bijection \(\varphi\) breaks the cubic
symmetry through taste-breaking at \(\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^2)\), with the
hierarchy emerging from the second-order perturbative structure.

The \emph{existence} of a hierarchy is structural --- any bijection
\(\varphi\) breaking the cubic symmetry produces a hierarchy. The
\emph{pattern} of the hierarchy --- which generation is heaviest, the
specific mass ratios, the CKM mixing angles --- is solution-specific,
requiring the specific properties of \(\varphi\) to derive. The
framework has an exact singlet-plus-triplet geometric decomposition;
interpreting the triplet as three physical generations requires H-link
single-copy together with H-spin', and the specific pattern is the open
task developed in §19.3.1 (the flavor problem).

\emph{Developed in:} Chapter 6 §§6.5 and 6.6, with the flavor open
problem at §19.3.1 below.

\hypertarget{the-dark-sector-budget}{%
\subsubsection{19.2.11 The dark sector
budget}\label{the-dark-sector-budget}}

\textbf{Standard status.} Why is the universe approximately \(5\%\)
baryonic, \(27\%\) dark matter, and \(68\%\) dark energy? No
conventional framework explains these ratios from first principles. The
dark sector's \(\sim 95\%\) total is treated as empirical input.

\textbf{Framework status.} The horizon first law and boundary count give
the thermal energy used in the comparison. Its Hubble-volume mean is
\(\rho_s=3c^2H^2/(8\pi G)\) in three spatial dimensions, equal to the
supplied flat Friedmann density. The equality concerns the average. The
physical source requires the open covariant coupling. {[}GR §7.2{]}

If boundary entropy accounts for the nonbaryonic source, the supplied
baryon fraction leaves \(1-\Omega_B\) for its contribution. The split
into matter-like and vacuum-like parts near \(27\%\) and \(68\%\)
remains open.

\emph{Developed in:} Chapter 7 §7.9.

\hypertarget{the-origin-of-the-born-rule}{%
\subsubsection{19.2.12 The origin of the Born
rule}\label{the-origin-of-the-born-rule}}

\textbf{Standard status.} The Born rule --- that the probability of
measuring quantum state \(|x\rangle\) given wave function
\(|\psi\rangle\) is \(|\langle x | \psi \rangle|^2\) --- is an
independent postulate of quantum mechanics with no derivation from the
other axioms. Gleason's theorem derives the Born rule from
non-contextuality, but non-contextuality is itself a postulate. The
various interpretive programs (many-worlds, QBism, Bohmian, dynamical
collapse) take different positions on what the Born rule means without
explaining why it has the specific form
\(|\langle x | \psi \rangle|^2\).

\textbf{Framework status.} Split --- fixed-basis representation settled
exactly; coherent operational extension characterized by five
conditions. Every finite-horizon stochastic law has an exact fixed-basis
unitary/Born representation (\(S\iff D\iff Q_{\mathrm{fb}}\), {[}Main
§3.4{]}); in that theorem the quadratic Born dictionary is part of the
equivalent representation, not a separate exponent-selection problem.
The further question begins when one asks for \textbf{one common
operational theory} covering arbitrary coherent preparations,
noncommuting effects/instruments, and composites. Main's finite response
table realizes the supplied quantum probabilities for a fixed
preparation, instrument menu and horizon. The finite instrument net
extends coverage to arbitrary finite accuracy at fixed initial state.
The same response-table machinery can also realize non-quantum finite
behaviors. The operational-completion characterization ({[}GR §3.3{]})
states exactly which conditions select the quantum ones --- valid
probabilities, trivial-ancilla consistency, inert spectators, full
reversible control, and iterated composition --- each independent of the
others and of the observation process, so that embedded observation by
itself does not select quantum mechanics and the physical question is
which of those conditions the substratum supplies. The characterization
takes complex matrix kinematics as given --- operations act on the
complex matrices indexed by the configurations of the system and of its
composites --- and deriving that kinematics is a further open question.
Its layered form, quantum-complete OI (OI⁺) --- the unchanged OI core
with well-formedness, observational independence, reversible richness,
and observer recursion --- is equivalent on every nonempty finite
carrier to exact finite endomorphic operational quantum mechanics, with
no claim that bare OI entails the added principles ({[}GR §3.3{]}). A
primitive-source refinement of that layered form restates the three
principles at the level of physical implementations and embedded
observers --- implementation locality, phase-free richness --- one
continuously driven transition and the exchanges of distinguishable
states, with no phase operation --- and embedded observation, with no
closure of the implementations under the adjoint and no inverse
accessibility assumed --- equivalent to the same operational quantum
mechanics on every nonempty finite carrier ({[}GR §3.3{]}). A
substratum-source form completes that refinement: the concrete OI
substratum, in its finite model (ledger item (ii)), supplies the
structural architecture --- closure under composition and
coarse-graining, stability under an uncoupled spectator, relabelling
invariance, reversibility, the exchanges of distinguishable states, and,
as a stated intervention principle rather than a consequence of its
finite states and bijective dynamics, the phases --- but, under finite
bijective read-write dynamics as represented by the specified monomial
implementation class, elementary drivability fails, and the generated
theory on the two-state carrier lacks composite unitary control. A
structurally closed extension with elementary drivability generates
exact finite endomorphic operational quantum mechanics on every nonempty
finite carrier. In the memory-swap example, a nontrivial exchange of the
selected states has a monomial operator ({[}GR §3.3{]}). Its typed form
removes the endomorphic qualifier: under the carrier-general typed
operational interface --- identity, composition, coarse-graining,
relabelling, uniform finite attachment, discard, and factor readout, an
interface that itself carries no quantum content --- the same
equivalence holds with exact finite-dimensional typed operational
quantum mechanics, operations between any two nonempty finite carriers
included, so the remaining qualifier is finite-dimensional rather than
endomorphic ({[}GR §3.3{]}). The finite theory admits a canonical
infinite-region completion without a continuum limit: the finite regions
of the fixed-spacing lattice carry full matrix algebras joined by
compatible injective unital embeddings with observables of disjoint
regions commuting, the norm completion of their union is a quasilocal
\(C^{*}\)-algebra on which every consistent family of finite-region
density matrices is a state and the reversible finite-range substratum
update is an isometric \(*\)-automorphism, and any system carrying the
same local stages is canonically and uniquely \(*\)-isomorphic to it,
intertwining the dynamics; this removes the finite-region cutoff for the
algebra, the state space, and the OI-induced discrete dynamics rather
than characterizing all infinite-dimensional quantum instruments or all
locality-preserving quantum dynamics; the lattice spacing stays
fundamental, no Hilbert-space representation and no superselection
sector is selected at the level of the laws, the restriction to the
substratum-induced dynamics is a theorem rather than a convention --- a
phase automorphism at one site preserves locality without arising from
any reversible finite-range bijection --- and, while the update is
joined to the identity by an exact strongly continuous path of
\(*\)-automorphisms of that algebra, with no one-parameter-group law
established and no generator exhibited, a continuous-time Hamiltonian
law remains additional structure ({[}GR §3.3{]}). Within the structural
architecture the substratum supplies, with the phase intervention
stated, exact finite endomorphic operational quantum mechanics holds
exactly when one continuous layer flow of an involution of the
configuration space moving some configuration is an available operation
at every level and every intermediate time, the executability of that
flow being an assumption not derived by configuration-level generation,
as the phase intervention is an assumption on the substratum class and
not a consequence of the finite states with the bijective dynamics
({[}GR §3.3{]}). The stated substratum dynamics with the observer's read
and write access do not source that executability, the layers being
available at time one and not at intermediate times, and the
observer-level lift, in every formulation stated that lands in the
operational interface, derives neither a non-monomial admissible
operator nor the layer flow, the site-space wave-operator formulation
being unresolved rather than excluded ({[}GR §3.3{]}). The cosmological
realization adds a mechanism proposal --- the equilibrium reading of the
read-write cycle (Chapter 18 §18.2) --- whose stationary-distribution
step is a structural commitment rather than a premise of the
representation theorem.

The mechanism proposal of Chapter 18 §18.2 implies transient deviations
from the Born rule in the very early universe if the hidden sector began
away from equilibrium, relaxing on a timescale the proposal identifies
with the hidden sector's equilibration time; that timescale sets the
order of the relaxation rate, while the form of the decay requires in
addition a closed relaxation law and its rate coefficient, neither of
which is derived. Their observational reach depends on the source
dynamics, the family of initial deviations and the map to the CMB's
primordial power spectrum and non-Gaussianity, which the proposal does
not yet fix; CMB measurements of those statistics are the channel in
which they would be tested once these are fixed.

\textbf{Two frontiers, not one.} The split recorded above concerns the
\emph{operational} extension: which conditions select one common theory
of coherent preparations, instruments and composites, answered
conditionally by the completion principles. A second and separate
question is left open by that answer --- which unitary evolution relates
one time to the next, given a visible OI family that admits several
coherent lifts. Ordinary coherence does not settle it, and the
completion characterization does not address it. That frontier is
recorded at §19.3.9; the two should not be read as one residue.

\emph{Developed in:} Chapter 1, with forward content in Chapter 18
§18.2.

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\hypertarget{problems-open-within-the-framework}{%
\subsection{19.3 Problems open within the
framework}\label{problems-open-within-the-framework}}

This section develops the seven entries the framework does not fully
resolve --- the five standard open problems counted in the headline
inventory, plus two framework-specific items internal to the framework
rather than to the seventeen standard problems: the chirality hypothesis
H-χ' (§19.3.8), internal to the Standard-Model identification, and the
selection of the relative quantum evolution (§19.3.9), internal to the
OI--QM bridge. Neither framework-specific item changes the count of
standard open problems. Each entry pairs the standard formulation, the
framework's current status, an assessment of what remains open, and a
note on the prospects for closing the open question.

\hypertarget{the-flavor-problem}{%
\subsubsection{19.3.1 The flavor problem}\label{the-flavor-problem}}

\textbf{Standard status.} Why do fermion masses span five orders of
magnitude, with \(m_e/m_t \sim 3 \times 10^{-6}\)? Why the specific
pattern of CKM and PMNS mixing angles? Why the Koide relation
\(Q = (m_e + m_\mu + m_\tau)/(\sqrt{m_e} + \sqrt{m_\mu} + \sqrt{m_\tau})^2 = 2/3\)
to better than \(0.001\%\)? The Standard Model accommodates the fermion
masses as 13 free parameters; no conventional framework derives them.

\textbf{Framework status.} Open with a defined research program and
initial computational results. The fermion masses are taste-breaking
parameters of the substratum bijection \(\varphi\) --- properties of how
the specific \(\varphi\) breaks the cubic symmetry. The structural input
\(1/\alpha_0 = 23.25\) is computed from the one-loop staggered vacuum
polarization, and the three gauge couplings at \(M_Z\) are reproduced
with three matched threshold parameters (Chapter 6 §6.4), showing that
solution-specific parameters are constrainable in principle. The
research program identifies three tractable open targets.

\emph{The bottom-to-tau mass ratio.} The framework predicts
\(y_b = y_\tau\) at tree level --- the staggered taste-breaking is
diagonal in the gauge index. Full Standard Model RGE running (verified
against Luo and Xiao 2003) gives \(m_b/m_\tau|_{\text{tree}} = 4.276\)
from a common \(M_{\text{Pl}}\) boundary condition, indicating a
substantial non-perturbative correction. The full prediction including
the scalar-density renormalization \(Z_S\) from non-perturbative
dynamics at the matching scale is developed in Chapter 6 §6.6 (and SM
§7.5): with matching scale \(m_{\text{match}} = \lambda g_0^2 = 0.1217\)
derived structurally from the taste-decomposed Coleman-Weinberg
potential, and \(Z_S(m_{\text{match}}) = 1.813\) measured from Monte
Carlo at \(\beta = 11.1\) on \(L = 32\), the prediction is
\(m_b/m_\tau = 4.28/Z_S(m_{\text{match}}) = 2.361\) against the observed
\(2.352 \pm 0.017\) --- a \(0.4\%\) (\(0.5\sigma\)) match at \(L = 32\),
with \(L \to \infty\) extrapolation giving \(\sim 0.7\sigma\). The
\(L = 16\) Monte Carlo using only the \(\mathrm{SU}(3)\) mass
renormalization \(Z_m \approx 0.835\) at fixed bare mass --- the
calculation described in earlier versions of this section as giving
\(\sim 3.4\) (\(45\%\) off) --- corresponds to using the wrong matching
prescription rather than the wrong physics. With the correct matching
scale (a structural feature of the taste-decomposed CW potential rather
than a tunable parameter), the prediction matches observation at the
same level as the framework's other Layer 1 closures (Cabibbo, Koide,
\(\sin^2\theta_{13}\)). The kinematic prefactor
\(K = 1/(n_{\text{gen}} - 1) = 1/2\) is a Layer-1 structural identity
given the matching condition (\(c_{bb} = (n_{\text{gen}}-1)\lambda\));
its support is the Monte Carlo verification at \(1.4\%\)
(\(K_{\text{MC}} = 0.507\)). The explicit one-loop evaluation has been
carried out and cannot close the gap: in the condensate-ratio
construction the one-loop coefficient is \(0.446\)
(tadpole-normalization bracket \(0.393\)--\(0.446\)), \(11\)--\(21\%\)
below \(1/2\) at a coupling where \(Z_S - 1 = 0.81\) --- a truncation
error an order of magnitude larger than the MC precision, indicting the
truncation rather than the identity. Analytical closure requires the
resummed staggered-χPT chain or a non-perturbative identity, or
alternatively sub-percent MC; the task is Layer 2(a) in scope but not
one-loop in method (SM §7.5).

\emph{The Koide relation.} \(Q = 2/3\) is equivalent to the square-root
mass vector making a \(45°\) angle with the \([1, 1, 1]\) direction in
generation space --- equivalently, the amplitude \(A^2 = 2\) in the
\(\mathbb{Z}_3\) mass parametrization (SM §7.2). This has an exact
structural target: \(A^2 = C_2(T_1) = 2\), the same quadratic Casimir
that fixes the Koide angle \(\theta_0 = C_2/d^2\), so the amplitude and
the angle descend from one invariant. The open question is therefore
dynamical and sharper than ``whether the \(45°\) has a structural
origin'': one-loop perturbative taste-breaking gives
\(A^2 \approx 0.34\), so the task is to show that the non-perturbative
substrate dynamics produces \(A^2 = C_2 = 2\) --- a \({\sim}6\times\)
enhancement to a \emph{known} target --- via non-perturbative
enhancement of the \(E\)-component (the structural route, under which
the \(45°\) is derived) rather than solution-specific \(T_2\)
off-diagonal elements (under which it would be bijection-specific). The
full \(K = 6\) lattice Monte Carlo is the tool, and whether it lands on
\(C_2\) is the key open question. The observable class is constrained in
advance: an exact shift-symmetry identity makes the ensemble
single-quark two-point function eight-fold corner-degenerate at every
coupling, so quark-level taste splitting vanishes identically and the
measurement must use composite (multi-fermion) channels --- closing the
otherwise-natural quark-propagator route before it is attempted (SM
§7.2).

\emph{The Wolfenstein hierarchy.} Perturbative taste-breaking naturally
produces \(|V_{us}| \sim \lambda\), \(|V_{cb}| \sim \lambda^2\),
\(|V_{ub}| \sim \lambda^3\) --- the observed CKM pattern. The value
\(\lambda = 0.22508\) is the Cabibbo angle from cubic Brillouin geometry
(Chapter 6 §6.5 and Chapter 8 §8.3) --- a Tier 2 structural result. The
hierarchy pattern is therefore structurally fixed; the specific
magnitudes depend on the bijection.

\emph{Neutrino masses.} Majorana neutrinos, normal ordering, large PMNS
mixing, and a hierarchical spectrum are expected on the branch where the
singlet taste hosts the Higgs and no gauge-singlet fermion is present
(SM §8.4; the mechanism is otherwise open), the ordering and the
hierarchy as heuristic consequences of taste-breaking rather than
theorems (Chapter 6 §6.7 and Chapter 8). Specific mass values are
solution-specific.

\textbf{Required tools.} Full \(K = 6\) lattice Monte Carlo with the
scalar coupling matrix \(M = \mu I_6\) and the equivariant condensate
\(\Sigma\) (SM Theorem 5); representation theory of the cubic group
\(O\) applied to the framework's specific irrep content; 2-loop
lattice-to-continuum matching. Four C programs implementing the
perturbative taste-breaking spectrum, propagator-norm measurement,
effective-mass extraction, and taste-split correlators are available as
part of the framework's computational infrastructure.

\textbf{Assessment.} The flavor problem is the framework's largest
single open theoretical task. The framework has substantive content on
the \emph{structural form} of the flavor pattern (the existence of three
generations with hierarchical masses, the Cabibbo angle as Brillouin
geometry, the Wolfenstein hierarchy, normal ordering for neutrinos) and
on several specific magnitudes that are conditional structural at Layer
1 with one named open link each (Cabibbo \(\lambda\), Koide \(Q\),
\(\sin^2\theta_{13}\)) or layered --- \(m_b/m_\tau\) with a Layer 2(a)
verification residual, \(\sin^2\theta_{12}\) and \(\sin^2\theta_{23}\)
on a Layer 2(b) substrate coefficient (SM §7.6). The remaining
solution-specific parameters (specific CP phases, the full Yukawa
pattern beyond hierarchy existence) are bijection-specific in the
framework's terms --- structurally predicted \emph{not} to be derivable
from substrate alone, consistent with the framework's
observational-incompleteness commitment. The Layer 2(a) verification
residual is a tractable open task with a defined computational path; the
bijection-specific parameters are pre-registered as outside the
framework's substrate-derivable scope.

\hypertarget{the-hubble-tension}{%
\subsubsection{19.3.2 The Hubble tension}\label{the-hubble-tension}}

\textbf{Standard status.} The Hubble constant measured from the CMB
(Planck: \(H_0 = 67.4 \pm 0.5\) km/s/Mpc) disagrees with the local
distance ladder (SH0ES: \(H_0 = 73.0 \pm 1.0\) km/s/Mpc) at greater than
\(5\sigma\). The disagreement has persisted across multiple measurement
systematics, suggesting either an unidentified systematic in one or both
methods or new physics modifying the cosmic expansion history.

\textbf{Framework status.} Open. The near-null Type II model of §19.2.4
uses a conditional field estimate of order \(10^{-32}\). Its running is
negligible at current precision on the stated source and spectral
assumptions.

Quantifying any change in the inferred \(H_0\) requires a specified,
consistently sourced expansion model and a fit to the relevant data.

\textbf{Assessment.} A working explanation of the Hubble tension through
this coupling remains open. The conditional near-null model gives a
late-time comparison close to \(\Lambda\)CDM at the precision relevant
to the tension.

\hypertarget{baryogenesis}{%
\subsubsection{19.3.3 Baryogenesis}\label{baryogenesis}}

\textbf{Standard status.} The observed baryon-to-photon ratio
\(\eta = (6.1 \pm 0.2) \times 10^{-10}\) requires a mechanism to produce
a matter-antimatter asymmetry satisfying Sakharov's three conditions:
baryon number violation, C and CP violation, and out-of-equilibrium
dynamics. The conventional candidates --- electroweak baryogenesis, GUT
baryogenesis, leptogenesis through heavy right-handed neutrinos, and
various extensions --- have not been confirmed empirically.

\textbf{Framework status.} Solution-specific. The framework does not
derive the baryon-to-photon ratio and does not carry an obligation to
--- for the same structural reason it does not derive the CKM phase.
This status is the conclusion of a sustained investigation; the
reasoning is given below, and the honest record of that retraction is
part of the framework's content.

\textbf{Leptogenesis through the Weinberg operator.} The comparison on
the Majorana branch uses the Weinberg operator
\((c_{ij}/\Lambda) L_i L_j H H\), a hierarchical spectrum and supplied
CP-violating phases. The physical source of a complex lepton phase
remains open (Juno §3.3). The operator mediates \(\Delta L = 2\)
scattering in thermal equilibrium at \(T > 10^{14}\) GeV. A precise
calculation reveals a quantitative shortfall: the total unflavored CP
asymmetry vanishes by CPT plus unitarity
(\(\sum_\alpha \epsilon_\alpha = 0\)), and the surviving flavored
asymmetry from thermal corrections is suppressed by
\(y_\tau^2 \sim 5 \times 10^{-5}\), yielding
\(\eta_B \sim 4 \times 10^{-11}\) --- approximately \(15\times\) below
the observed value of \(6.1 \times 10^{-10}\). This is the same
shortfall faced by any framework with Majorana neutrinos but no heavy
right-handed neutrinos: the Weinberg operator alone, without a UV
completion providing additional CP-violating phases, cannot produce
sufficient baryon asymmetry.

\textbf{A retracted mechanism.} An earlier treatment proposed closing
the factor-15 gap with \emph{substratum-level instanton-like processes}
--- configurations of the bijection \(\varphi\) at the lattice cutoff
with action \(S \sim O(1)\), giving a suppression \(e^{-O(1)}\) rather
than the electroweak \(e^{-2\pi/\alpha_W}\). This mechanism is
\textbf{retracted}, and the reason is structural rather than
quantitative. The substratum has no Euclidean action functional: it is
the deterministic linear bijection of the wave-equation update rule
(Chapter 2), not a path-integral system. ``Substratum-level instantons
with action \(S \sim O(1)\)'' is therefore type-mismatched with what the
substratum is --- there is no action whose minima would constitute
instantons. The correct picture is the one Chapter 6's treatment of
baryon number already gives: substratum-level \(B\) is conserved at the
bilinear level, and non-perturbative \(B+L\) violation enters through
the \emph{emergent} fermion-determinant topology governed by standard
sphaleron physics. There is no additional substratum-level
baryon-number-violating channel.

\textbf{Why baryogenesis is solution-specific.} With the retracted
mechanism removed, the framework's relation to baryogenesis is settled
by a commitment the framework makes elsewhere and independently. The
substratum is T-symmetric --- this is load-bearing for the reciprocity
result of §19.2.7, which does not by itself fix \(\bar\theta\). Observed
CP violation in the CKM and PMNS sectors is, in the framework, a
flavor-basis feature of the \emph{specific bijection} \((S, \varphi)\)
--- not a derived quantity. The framework makes no prediction of
\(\delta_{\text{CKM}}\), \(\delta_{\text{PMNS}}\), or the Wolfenstein
\((\rho, \eta)\); these are treated as solution-specific inputs, in the
same category as the framework's choice of discretization scheme.

The baryon asymmetry inherits this status. Sakharov's second condition
is CP violation, and the only CP violation available to the framework is
exactly the flavor-sector CP it treats as a solution-specific input. A
quantity downstream of an input is itself an input: \(\eta_B\) is no
more derivable, within the framework's current commitments, than
\(\delta_{\text{CKM}}\) is. Demanding that the framework dynamically
\emph{generate} \(\eta_B\) from a symmetric initial condition holds it
to a standard it does not adopt for the CP phases \(\eta_B\) depends on.
The ``factor-15 open problem'' framing was an artifact of that
inconsistency.

\textbf{Assessment.} Baryogenesis is \emph{solution-specific}, not a
quantitative gap awaiting a mechanism. The framework's structural
ingredients (sphaleron \(B+L\) violation, the out-of-equilibrium
expanding early universe, the CKM/PMNS CP phases) are consistent with
the observed \(\eta_B\); what the framework does not do is derive its
value, because that value is downstream of CP phases the framework
inputs rather than derives. This is a reclassification that restores
internal consistency --- the framework no longer carries baryogenesis as
an unmet derivation obligation while simultaneously inputting
\(\delta_{\text{CKM}}\) --- and it is honest about its limits: it is not
a closure. It does not produce \(\eta_B = 6.1 \times 10^{-10}\) from
first principles, and a reader may fairly regard a framework that
derives the Cabibbo angle but inputs the baryon asymmetry as incomplete
in scope. The framework's position is that this incompleteness is
shared, explicit, and located precisely: it is the flavor-sector CP
input, named once and inherited wherever CP violation is needed.

\hypertarget{inflation-and-initial-conditions}{%
\subsubsection{19.3.4 Inflation and initial
conditions}\label{inflation-and-initial-conditions}}

\textbf{Standard status.} The horizon problem (why is the CMB isotropic
across causally disconnected regions?) and the flatness problem (why is
\(\Omega \approx 1\)?) are solved by an early period of exponential
expansion (inflation). But inflation requires a scalar field with a
specific potential, which is not part of the Standard Model. The initial
conditions for inflation are themselves fine-tuned. The empirical
evidence for inflation comes through CMB polarization measurements and
the absence of relics that pre-inflation cosmologies would produce.

\textbf{Framework status.} Not addressed. The framework reproduces the
Standard Model structure but does not address the very early universe's
dynamics. Three possibilities exist within the framework's structural
commitments, none of which has been developed in detail.

\emph{The Higgs as inflaton.} The framework accommodates an input Higgs
doublet; its existence and hypercharge are not derived (SM Theorem 11).
Higgs inflation (Bezrukov and Shaposhnikov, 2008) uses the Standard
Model Higgs with a non-minimal coupling \(\xi H^\dagger H R\) to drive
inflation. If the framework's Higgs \emph{is} the inflaton, inflation is
automatic --- but the non-minimal coupling \(\xi \sim 10^4\) is a
solution-specific parameter (a property of the bijection \(\varphi\)),
and its value is not determined by the framework's structural
commitments. The empirical predictions of Higgs inflation are
well-developed in the literature; whether the framework's bijection
produces \(\xi \sim 10^4\) is an open question requiring the full
bijection-specific calculation.

\emph{No inflation needed.} The framework's lattice structure may
resolve the horizon and flatness problems differently. On a finite
lattice, the notion of ``causally disconnected regions'' is modified ---
the lattice's coupling graph determines causal structure, and if the
initial state of \(\varphi\) is statistically isotropic (one of the
framework's six structural properties of the bijection), isotropy is
built in rather than requiring inflation to produce it. This is
speculative and would require a detailed analysis of the lattice's
causal structure at early times.

\emph{Initial conditions as gauge.} The deep hidden sector's cardinality
is gauge in the framework in the cases Chapter 2 §2.3 states. If the
initial state of the visible sector is also gauge-equivalent across a
wide class of initial conditions (because the trace-out erases the
distinction), then the ``initial conditions problem'' may dissolve
rather than require solution. This is an intriguing possibility but has
not been investigated within the framework's existing structure.

\textbf{Assessment.} Inflation is not derived, not refuted, and not
distinctively addressed by the framework. This is a genuine open problem
with the possibilities outlined but no current developed framework
position. Pre-registered: the framework's content on the very early
universe is one of the framework's most substantial scope limits in
fundamental physics.

\hypertarget{the-initial-state-of-s-varphi}{%
\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{19.3.5 The initial state of
\((S, \varphi)\)}{19.3.5 The initial state of (S, \textbackslash varphi)}}\label{the-initial-state-of-s-varphi}}

\textbf{Standard status.} Not applicable in the conventional sense ---
this is a framework-specific question. Why does the universe have the
particular bijection \(\varphi\) rather than some other? Why these
particular initial conditions for the bijection's evolution?

\textbf{Framework status.} Partially addressed, partially outside scope.
The reconstruction theorem establishes --- under its stated modeling,
mixing and nearest-neighbor premises --- uniqueness only of the
\textbf{local propagating lattice/gauge residue}. The Bell-inclusive
full substratum remains underdetermined: H-Bell conditions the existence
of the adopted preparation-indexed Bell completion, and uniqueness of
that Bell-composite rule remains open. The question ``why this
\(\varphi\)?'' therefore has a gauge-local layer and an additional
Bell-completion layer.

\emph{Within the reconstructed local equivalence class.} Gauge --- no
answer is physically required for representative choices that Theorem 24
identifies as observably equivalent. This statement does not identify
all Bell-inclusive completions with one another.

\emph{Why this equivalence class rather than another.} The framework's
axioms --- deterministic bijectivity, causal partition, classical
probability --- together with the open hypothesis A1 of finiteness
constrain the class. The framework's six structural properties of the
bijection (developed across Chapters 5-7) further narrow it. But the
axioms themselves are not derived from anything deeper.

The existence question --- ``why does \((S, \varphi)\) exist at all?''
--- is the framework's irreducible mystery. The framework's structural
account: \((S, \varphi)\) is a mathematical structure that cannot fail
to be well-defined; existence is the default for logically consistent
structures. Whether one finds this answer satisfying is a philosophical
question rather than a physical one. The framework's commitment is that
the existence of \emph{some} deterministic bijection structure (finite
under A1) is not a question physics can answer, while the existence of
\emph{this particular} structure (as determined by the empirical record)
is a constraint on which bijections are compatible with observation.

\textbf{Assessment.} The framework identifies this question as the only
genuinely irreducible mystery --- not a gap in the framework's reach but
the boundary of all possible frameworks. Any framework must take some
structural axioms as given; the framework's content is to make those
axioms as minimal and as structural as possible (deterministic
bijectivity, on a finite set under A1, no further commitments), leaving
the existence question as an explicit acknowledgment of where physics
ends.

\hypertarget{is-the-discrete-structural-residue-genuinely-non-tautological}{%
\subsubsection{19.3.6 Is the discrete structural residue genuinely
non-tautological?}\label{is-the-discrete-structural-residue-genuinely-non-tautological}}

\textbf{Standard status.} A framework-specific meta-question. The
reconstruction theorem sends the empirical and structural axioms to a
discrete residue --- the spatial dimension \(d=3\), the internal
multiplicity \(K=2d=6\), the gauge group
\(\mathrm{SU}(3)\times\mathrm{SU}(2)\times\mathrm{U}(1)\), three
generations, the hypercharges. The question is whether these are forced
and could have been otherwise (substantive content), or whether they are
already contained in the inputs and the derivation unpacks them
(tautological).

\textbf{Framework status.} Resolved --- not by a calculation, but by
recognizing that the question is mis-posed. It presupposes a single
yes/no answer for ``the residue,'' but the residue is not uniform: its
members have three different logical statuses, and once they are
separated the question has a definite answer for each. \emph{Tier 1 ---
forced by representation theory (genuinely non-tautological).} Given the
simple-cubic lattice and the wave equation, the multiplicities
\((3,2,1)\) follow from the octahedral character table with no further
freedom, and, on the carrier branch of H-link and H-cust, the gauge
factors, the generation count of three (as physical generations under
H-spin'), the anomaly-free hypercharges (on the nonzero-\(Y_Q\) branch,
up to normalization), and, under its identification hypothesis, the
Cabibbo angle follow from it and anomaly analysis; they could \emph{a
priori} have come out otherwise, and the predictive excess noted above
(the Cabibbo angle, Koide, the PMNS angles, six mass ratios --- none of
them among the empirical inputs) is exactly the signature of genuine
content. This tier is real and substantial. \emph{Tier 2 --- empirically
selected.} Two of the listed invariants are \emph{not} forced by the
construction: \(d=3\) is selected by the three
Standard-Model-independent filters (§3.2 of the SM paper), and the
simple-cubic Bravais structure is selected, under nearest-neighbor
coupling, by the observed
\(\mathrm{SU}(3) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{U}(1)\) --- only
the cubic crystal system supplies the three-dimensional point-group
irrep an \(\mathrm{SU}(3)\) factor needs (Theorem 7b). For these the
inference runs from the observed world back to the commitment; ``the
Standard Model from a cubic lattice'' and ``the lattice is cubic because
we observe \(\mathrm{SU}(3)\)'' are one fact stated in two directions.
The threshold \(\delta_0\) and the absolute mass scales are likewise
empirical. \emph{Tier 3 --- stipulation.} Site factorization (the
identification of sites, which the dynamics has not been shown to select
and coupling-degree minimization does not), the single-copy clause of
H-link (from which \(K=2d\) follows), the nearest-neighbor restriction,
and the C1--C4 architecture itself are choices about what counts as
physical structure rather than facts the bijection forces; they are
principled, but they are stipulations.

\textbf{Assessment.} The meta-question is therefore not open pending
computation --- no lattice calculation moves it, because the status of
each link is already fixed by the construction as written. It is
answered by the classification: non-tautological at Tier 1,
tautological-in-the-relevant-sense at Tier 2, definitional at Tier 3.
Several distinct concerns --- the derived-versus-input ledger, the
residual-input status of Lorentz structure (§19.3.7 and the boost sector
of the SM paper), and the circularity question --- reduce to this one
and are resolved the same way. The constructive consequence is a precise
statement of what the framework is: a \emph{maximally tight compression}
of observed physics onto the cubic-lattice commitment. Tier 1
establishes that, once the commitment is granted, the Standard Model's
discrete structure is largely not independent --- it is a single
representation-theoretic object --- which is a genuine and unusual claim
about the unity of physics. Tiers 2--3 establish that the commitment
itself is empirically anchored and partly stipulated, so the framework
does not derive physics from a parameter-free first principle. The
earlier framing of this as ``open, not closable by internal means''
mistook a question about the \emph{logical status of the construction's
steps} --- which the construction already answers --- for a question
awaiting evidence. The proposed external calibration against the
operational reconstruction theorems of quantum theory (Hardy;
Masanes--Müller; Chiribella--D'Ariano--Perinotti) remains a worthwhile
comparison, but it bears on how to \emph{value} a ``uniquely-fixed''
result, not on whether the present residue is forced; the latter is
settled above. (The three-tier classification is developed in full in
{[}SM §8.3{]} and {[}Substratum §3, Refinement{]}; its bearing on the
framework's foundational claim is drawn out in {[}Structure §13.4, Limit
4{]}.)

\hypertarget{radiative-stability-of-emergent-lorentz-invariance-rotational-sector}{%
\subsubsection{19.3.7 Radiative stability of emergent Lorentz invariance
(rotational
sector)}\label{radiative-stability-of-emergent-lorentz-invariance-rotational-sector}}

Two results bear on this question. A symmetric-integration argument
shows that an exactly \(O_h\)-invariant action, measure, and
observer-centered partition yield an \(O_h\)-invariant effective theory
to all orders, and every ingredient of the checkerboard trace-out is
\(O_h\)-invariant --- no direction-dependent momentum shell is
available. A numerical check on the rounded interacting dynamics, whose
code and numerical output are not available for verification (extraction
reported validated against the analytic tree coefficients to the percent
level; the allowed \(\ell=4\) anisotropy reported detected at high
significance), reported the forbidden \(E_g\) coefficient zero within
errors at the \(2\times10^{-5}\) level in the perturbative regime and
consistent with zero in the thermalized strong-coupling state.
Separately, the sector-differential boost violation's custodial
decoupling law --- conditional on the symmetric-point matching under
H-blind ({[}SM §4.4{]}) --- has its normalization bounded
(\(\Delta C_2 \in [0.58, 2.08]\) from the framework's representation
content), and its decoupling form, controls and kernel constants
(\(c_L \simeq -9.4\), \(d \simeq -0.88\)) reported by a one-loop
calculation whose driver and numerical output are not available for
verification; on that reported form the worst-case \(\Delta C_2\) would
give an \(M_X\) window of two to five orders of magnitude against the
tightest multi-species bounds, an intermediate scale \(\lesssim 10^8\)
GeV, narrowing with the reported constants and the representation-side
point values to a ceiling of \(\sim 4\times10^{7}\) GeV and a window of
one and a half to four and a half decades --- illustrative figures
carrying the provenance of that calculation ({[}SM §3.1{]}). What
remains: production-scale statistics, the \(\ell=4\) alignment of the
observer-position boundary anisotropy, and the cross-charged
phenomenology floor. See {[}SM §3.1{]} for the full statements.

\textbf{Standard status.} The Lorentz fine-tuning problem familiar from
effective-field-theory treatments of Planck-scale Lorentz violation:
tree-level suppression of Lorentz-violating operators need not survive
radiative corrections.

\textbf{Framework status.} Open. The sector-\emph{differential}
(inter-species) boost-violation is addressed in two steps: at the
matching scale the signed-permutation symmetry of the carrier components
makes the quadratic response custodially scalar under H-blind ({[}SM
§4.4{]}, Proposition 4b), and below it the custodial-\(\mathrm{U}(6)\)
mechanism gives a power-law-with-logarithm decoupling in the heavy
cross-charged mass whose form was reported by a one-loop calculation
that is not independently verified (SM §3.1 (\emph{Scope of the
emergent-Lorentz claim}), F13). The remaining gap is the
\emph{sector-common} operator in the rotational sector, which has no
analogous power-law suppression and depends on the
renormalization-group-emergence (operator-smearing) mechanism, whose
inter-species flow is only logarithmically fast. This rotational
sub-problem does not reduce to §19.3.6 (it is a technical
radiative-stability question rather than a question about the residue's
content). Closing it requires establishing that the emergent theory
preserves the octahedral symmetry at loop level: cubic symmetry and
locality place the rotational violation at dimension six (SM §3.1,
\emph{Scope of the emergent-Lorentz claim} point (iii) and \emph{A
present-day constraint, and the rotational sector's distinct status}),
so the residual question is loop-level octahedral invariance rather than
ultraviolet smearing.

\textbf{A framing note on the gauge hierarchy.} Several of the items
above can be stated in terms of the substratum gauge group
\(\mathcal{G}_{\text{sub}}\) --- the transformations preserving all
observables of \((S,\varphi)\). On this description each physical
quantity falls into one of three classes:
\(\mathcal{G}_{\text{sub}}\)-gauge and unobservable (quotiented away);
observable but solution-specific (the absolute mass scale, the CP
phases, the neutrino Yukawas --- properties of the particular
\(\varphi\)); and forced structural residue (the discrete quantities of
§19.3.6). The claim that quantum mechanics, gravity, and the Standard
Model are three projections of the one equivalence class
\([(S,\varphi)]/\mathcal{G}_{\text{sub}}\) is the framework's statement
of scope; the question of §19.3.6 is whether the third class has content
independent of the inputs.

\textbf{Low-energy questions about coarse-graining.} Rotational
protection, the boundary spectral weight and the stability of the
general-graph mode count each depend on properties of the low-energy
observer description. The reported free linear half-space result uses
the reconstructed wave operator and gives a boundary-projected
\(dN/d\omega\propto\omega^4\). Its extension to the interacting theory
and its attribution to the Type II source remain open. Deducing a common
signature in running, Lorentz violation and mode counting requires a map
relating the interacting observables. The even/odd grading descends
through the linear trace-out by the Schur-complement identity of {[}SM
§4.8{]}, with the interacting sector again a separate question.

\textbf{Why these particular features are inputs: constitution versus
consequence.} A natural question is why the open and input items cluster
as they do --- why, for instance, the framework derives (conditionally
on H-link) the gauge group and the generation count but must take the
spatial dimension, the cubic lattice, and (per §19.3.7) rotational
isotropy as inputs. The organizing principle is the distinction between
the \emph{constitution} of the substratum and its \emph{consequences}.
The framework derives the consequences of a given constitution --- the
anomaly-free hypercharges and the Cabibbo angle follow by representation
theory of the cubic group acting on the link directions, and the gauge
group and the three generations follow once H-link identifies those
links as the physical carrier, together with the trace-out, \emph{once
the substratum is fixed}. It does not derive the constitution itself ---
the dimension, the Bravais type, the rotational isotropy, the
periodicity. The reason is structural rather than incidental: an
embedded observer is built \emph{out of} the substratum, so it can have
leverage on the consequences of its own constitution but not on that
constitution prior to itself. The one qualification is that a
consequence which the framework cannot yet \emph{compute} is also booked
as an input on tractability grounds rather than principle (the threshold
\(\delta_0\) of §6.2 is the clearest case; it is a consequence of the
coupling-running, input only because it is not yet derived). With that
qualification the rule is clean: inputs comprise the substratum's
constitution together with any not-yet-tractable consequences, while the
derived results are the tractable consequences. This is offered as an
organizing observation, not a theorem; it is not claimed that
derivability coincides with any single formal property, and indeed the
largest block of derived results (the representation-theoretic ones)
would follow for any analyst of the fixed lattice, with no reference to
an observer at all.

\textbf{A note on the boost/rotation asymmetry specifically.} The split
between the two Lorentz sub-sectors of §19.3.7 --- the boost sector, for
which the framework has structural tools (the symmetric-point custodial
scalarity under H-blind, the custodial-\(\mathrm{U}(6)\) mechanism, the
local-boost-invariance prerequisite of the Jacobson construction, the
vacuum-Cherenkov stability filter), versus the rotational sector, which
has no analogous ally --- tracks this same constitution/consequence
distinction through a specific feature of embedded observation. The
trace-out is realized at a causal horizon, and that horizon
\emph{singles out a rest frame} (the frame in which the substratum
update steps are simultaneous, identified in §7 with the cosmic rest
frame). The observation map therefore makes contact with boost structure
--- the horizon partition defining it distinguishes a temporal
direction, which is what boosts act on --- and this is why the boost
sector admits framework-level arguments. It does not single out any
spatial direction; spatial isotropy is a property of the lattice
constitution, untouched by the rest-frame selection. This is formalized
as the rest-frame-selection lemma of {[}Main §3.5{]} (given that the
observation map determines its foliation, its invariances exclude boosts
and, among orthochronous transformations, lie within the little group
\(O(3)\) of its selected timelike direction; which rotations are
invariances depends on the substratum dynamics and the lattice geometry
of the partition, not on the rest-frame selection). On this reading the
relative tractability of the boost sector and the input status of the
rotational sector are not separate facts but two faces of the
rest-frame-selecting character of embedded observation: the rest-frame
selection touches what distinguishes time from space (boosts), and is
silent on what distinguishes one spatial direction from another
(rotations). This is an interpretive observation about why the
open-problem boundary falls where it does, not an additional technical
result.

\textbf{The rotational sector as a structural question about
observational incompleteness.} The boost/rotation note above and the
smearing question of §19.3.7 can be drawn together into a single
statement about \emph{why} the rotational sector is the one that resists
protection --- and the statement is a structural feature of embedded
observation itself, not an incidental gap. The protection the rotational
sector would need is a sufficient operator-smearing: a coarse-graining
whose kernel damps ultraviolet spatial modes (so the
radiatively-generated anisotropy stays suppressed). The framework's
coarse-graining is the trace-out, and the trace-out \emph{is} the
observational incompleteness --- the observer's ignorance of the hidden
sector. The crucial point is \emph{what kind} of incompleteness this is.
By the fluctuation discriminant of {[}Main §3.5{]}, the trace-out
averages over the hidden \emph{state} --- over which microstate the slow
bath occupies --- not over spatial scale. A state-average is not a
spatial ultraviolet filter: averaging over which microstate the bath is
in does nothing to remove short-wavelength spatial modes, since those
are present in every microstate alike. The framework's incompleteness is
moreover enormous --- the slow-bath capacity ratio
\(\tau_B/\tau_S \sim 10^{32}\) is the engine of the entire
quantum-emergence result --- but it is incompleteness \emph{about a
temporally-evolving state}, concentrated in the state and (through the
slow bath) temporal directions. It is silent in the spatial direction in
the same way, and for the same reason, that the rest-frame selection of
the lemma is silent on spatial axes.

This can be made quantitative. The smearing kernel is the traced-out
hidden-sector propagator \(G_{oo}\) ({[}SM §4.8{]}); its position-space
width is the smearing radius \(R\). A direct computation of that width
on the cubic lattice gives a width \(R\) of about a single lattice
spacing --- and, decisively, that width is \emph{flat} as the slow-bath
ratio \(\tau_B/\tau_S\) is varied across thirty orders of magnitude. The
framework's vast observational incompleteness contributes \emph{nothing}
to the spatial smearing width; the only spatial smearing present is the
order-one multi-site support of the staggered reconstruction, which is
far too narrow (\(R/\varepsilon = \mathcal{O}(1)\), not \(\gg 1\)) to
damp the ultraviolet. This is the structural reason the smearing route
does not add ultraviolet damping to the rotational sector --- and it is
why the available computations (static, free-dynamical, and one-loop)
find \(R/\varepsilon = \mathcal{O}(1)\) rather than
\(R \gg \varepsilon\): the incompleteness is the wrong \emph{kind} to
UV-damp, regardless of its magnitude. Whether the absence of smearing
leaves the sector \emph{unprotected}, however, depends on the dimension
analysis below.

Three of the framework's findings thus share one root. The
rest-frame-selection lemma (the horizon partition defining the map
selects a timelike direction, no spatial one, and the map excludes
boosts when it determines the horizon foliation), the fluctuation
discriminant (the map averages the fluctuating state, not the fixed
orientation), and the smearing-width result (the incompleteness has
order-one spatial width independent of its magnitude) are three
expressions of a single fact: \emph{observational incompleteness in this
framework is incompleteness about a temporally-evolving hidden state,
with purchase on time, boost, and state, and structurally silent on
space and rotation.} The rotational sector is precisely the sector
embedded observation cannot reach. The valence of this account is
narrower than it first appears. The smearing-width result it establishes
--- that observational incompleteness adds no ultraviolet spatial
smearing, so \(R\) is about one lattice spacing --- bears on the
\emph{coefficient} of the rotational operator, not its \emph{dimension}.
The dimension is fixed independently, by the octahedral selection rule
(the \(E_g\) anisotropy is a cubic non-singlet; the lowest invariant
anisotropy is \(\ell=4\), dimension six) together with locality, and a
direct tree-level computation confirms the emergent dispersion
anisotropy is \(\sim(\varepsilon k)^2 \propto (E/M_{\text{Pl}})^2\). The
account therefore explains why embedded observation does not
\emph{smear} the rotational sector, but smearing is not what the sector
needs: cubic symmetry and locality already place the violation at
dimension six, Planck-suppressed. What remains genuinely open is the
loop-level question --- whether the emergent theory preserves the
octahedral symmetry \emph{exactly}, or whether the emergence introduces
an octahedral-breaking effect not visible in the bare partition.

This premise has a second dependency alongside the partition. The
effective theory is octahedrally invariant only if the condensate that
breaks the framework's custodial symmetry is itself aligned to the cubic
axes; the invariance of the dynamics does not descend to the solution,
since the gauge group arises precisely by that condensate breaking a
symmetry the dynamics has. The alignment is not secured by the observed
gauge group alone --- a condensate with the same block sizes but
misaligned eigenspaces yields the same gauge group without being
octahedrally equivariant, so the equivariance argument that forbids the
anisotropy below dimension six does not cover it --- and it is not
derived: it is the hypothesis that the matter-content and mixing-angle
results also take, namely H-link with its single-copy clause, the open
hypothesis that the physical carrier is one copy of the six-link
representation (Chapter 5 §5.4), together with an octahedrally
equivariant condensate, whose blocks are then the link-direction irreps
(Chapter 5 §5.5). An aligned condensate leaves the forbidden anisotropy
exactly null at every block splitting, and a staggered spatial
modulation of the condensate does not lift it. See {[}SM §3.1{]}. This
has an identifiable failure point: it assumes the visible/hidden
partition acts as a state/sublattice trace that preserves the octahedral
symmetry, rather than an effective short-wavelength (momentum-shell) cut
that could both ultraviolet-damp and, if anisotropic, break it. The
gaplessness of \(G_{oo}\) is evidence the partition is not a clean
momentum shell; whether it is exactly octahedral-invariant at loop level
is the seam at which the dimension-six protection could fail, and is the
arbiter --- not the kernel width. This premise is grounded in the
framework's own factorization criterion ({[}Main §3.1, §3.5{]}): an
observer-centered, horizon-isotropic partition is spherical and hence
octahedrally symmetric about the observer's centre, so the lattice
octahedral group --- unlike translations, boosts (when the map
determines the horizon foliation), and rotations about distant points,
which the partition breaks --- preserves the visible/hidden
factorization and descends to an exact symmetry of the effective theory.
With the partition exactly octahedral-invariant and the condensate
aligned (H-link with an equivariant condensate), the same criterion that
selects the gauge symmetries protects the rotational sector and exposes
the boost sector, so the dimension-six rotational protection and the
dimension-four boost exposure are two faces of one structural fact
rather than independent assumptions.

\hypertarget{the-chirality-hypothesis-h-ux3c7}{%
\subsubsection{19.3.8 The chirality hypothesis
H-χ'}\label{the-chirality-hypothesis-h-ux3c7}}

The Standard-Model identification carries one named structural
hypothesis. \textbf{H-χ':} a \emph{non-minimal} mechanism renders the
effective SU(2) coupling taste-chirality-selective. The minimal question
is settled: the link-current embeddings the construction delivers are
certified taste-blind for all three gauge blocks --- SU(3), SU(2), U(1)
alike --- by exact spin⊗taste classification
(\texttt{hchi\_selectivity\_probes.py}), so the minimal SU(2) is
vector-like and any selectivity must enter through a taste-asymmetric
structure (condensate/mass sector) in the Schur-complement effective
theory. What is proved, and probe-certified
(\texttt{chirality\_grading\_probes.py}): on the visible sector the
spin-chirality and taste-chirality operators coincide, so a gauge
coupling is spin-chiral there if and only if its embedding is
taste-chirality-selective (SM §4.8, Theorem 13); the grading itself is
\((d_L, d_R) = (4, 4)\) with \(\Gamma(0) = I_4\) chirality-neutral,
refuting the earlier ``even sublattice = left-handed'' identification;
SU(3) is vector-like; and the generation count does not depend on H-χ'.
What is open is H-χ' itself: whether the substratum's SU(2) embedding is
in fact taste-chirality-selective. The resolution path is a computation
in the framework's own representation machinery --- the embedding's
action on the graded components of the coupling matrix (the Theorem 7
apparatus). A computed non-selective embedding falsifies the chirality
identification, and with it the specific Standard-Model matter
assignment, while leaving the gauge group, the multiplicities
\((3, 2, 1)\), and the generation count intact; a computed selective
embedding discharges the hypothesis and upgrades the chirality clause
corpus-wide. The condition's standing status is transcribed in the
status ledger (Main §4.5).

\hypertarget{selection-of-the-relative-quantum-evolution}{%
\subsubsection{19.3.9 Selection of the relative quantum
evolution}\label{selection-of-the-relative-quantum-evolution}}

\textbf{Framework-specific.} This is not one of the standard open
problems; it is a frontier internal to the OI--QM bridge, and it is
recorded here so that the bridge's settled and unsettled parts are not
read as one thing.

\textbf{What is settled.} The finite-law bridge is solved at the level
of exact representability: every finite-horizon visible law has a finite
reversible realization and a fixed-basis unitary/Born representation,
and the three descriptions are equivalent
(\(S \iff D \iff Q_{\mathrm{fb}}\), {[}Main §3.4{]}). Separately, exact
finite operational quantum mechanics is characterized
\emph{conditionally}: within complex matrix kinematics taken as given,
it holds exactly when the explicit completion principles hold, none of
which bare embedded observation supplies ({[}GR §3.3{]}, §19.2.12).

\textbf{What is open.} Between those two lies a question neither
answers. A visible OI family does not come with a single unitary
evolution relating one time to the next: it admits coherent lifts, and
the lifts need not agree on that relating evolution. So the open
question is whether, and by what, one relative quantum evolution is
selected from the coherent lifts compatible with a single visible
family. The question is two-part: what selects or constrains, through
time, the fibre-Gram data of the lift --- for each visible output, the
overlaps among the hidden states into which the lift sends the visible
inputs --- and what fixes the relating evolution within a given
trajectory of that data.

\textbf{What is proved about it.} Ordinary coherence is not enough. Two
coherent lifts of the same visible family can be related by a
time-dependent deformation that preserves everything the visible law
sees, while their relating evolutions differ; a deformation constant in
time cancels from every relating evolution, so the nonuniqueness is
carried by time dependence specifically ({[}Main §3.4{]}). The invisible
deformations are two-sided --- a right action by the anchored class and
a left action within each visible output's hidden fibre, each maximal
among uniform actions of its kind --- and at one time the residue after
both is classified exactly: two lifts are related by the two-sided
action exactly when their fibre-Gram data agree up to phases, the
visible law is the diagonal of that data, and every positive
semidefinite, rank-bounded, identity-summing family with the prescribed
diagonal occurs. So the freedom the visible law leaves at one time is
exactly the off-diagonal fibre-Gram data modulo phases. At one time that
freedom does not reach the fixed-basis layer. With a trivial ancilla,
the fixed-basis datum built from a lift's unitary, with uniform initial
law and identity readout, has finite-horizon trajectory laws fixed by
the visible law alone, also after contractively scaled partial
permutations on either side, and two such data have equal laws exactly
